newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine bishop, bystander shot dead, 6 injured.
newsitem.headline: Philippine bishop, bystander shot dead, 6 injured.

text.p: A man and a boy possibly as young as 10 shot dead a Roman Catholic bishop on Tuesday in a flareup of violence against churchmen in a southern Philippine region racked by Moslem secessionist violence.
A church spokesman said Bishop Benjamin de Jesus died instantly when he was shot six times with .45 calibre pistols at point blank range near his cathderal on Jolo island.
A woman bystander was killed and five civilians were wounded when chasing police traded fire with the killers, who escaped through a crowd in a central Jolo town, army officials said.
Police said they had not established the identity of the assassins or the motive for the attack.
De Jesus, 56, was the highest church leader killed in a region where several foreign Catholic missionaries have been kidnapped and Catholic churches have been bombed in recent years.
The military attributed most of the violence to Moslem extremist groups fighting for an Islamic state in Asia's only largely Catholic nation.
In Manila, church spokesman Monsignor Pedro Quitorio called on Catholics to remain calm and urged them not to be provoked into reprisals.

"We are asking our priests to continue their work for reconciliation and peace and not to be intimidated," Quitorio said in a radio broadcast. "We are asking people not to meet violence with violence."
Jolo, about 900 km (560 miles) south of Manila, is one of the most volatile areas in the Mindanao region, the scene of a lingering Moslem secessionist movement.

The main rebel group, the Moro National Liberation Front (MNLF), reached a peace deal with the government last year. But hardline guerrillas, including the fundamentalist Abu Sayyaf group, still operate in the area.

"According to our priests in the area, the first gunman was between 30 and 40 years old while the second gunman was a boy between 10 and 15," Quitorio told Reuters. He said a third gunman acted as look-out.

Father Phil Estrella, a senior official of the religious congregation to which de Jesus belonged, said the bishop normally travelled with two Marine escorts after several churchmen received threats from extremist groups that they would be killed or kidnapped.
But on Tuesday, he was without the escorts, Estrella said by telephone.
Armed forces chief General Arnulfo Acedera ordered a hunt for the assassins.

Despite the peace deal with the MNLF, sporadic violence has continued in Mindanao, with 33 rebels of the breakaway Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF) and four soldiers killed in fierce fighting last month around Buldon town.
The government and the MILF are holding exploratory talks on a separate peace deal, but the Abu Sayyaf has shunned talks with Manila.

The military has blamed the Abu Sayyaf for the abduction of several foreign missionaries, mostly Americans, in the southern islands in recent years. It also blamed the Abu Sayyaf for the bombing of at least three Catholic churches last year.
Jolo is a predominantly Moslem island with a population of about 700,000, of whom about 20,000 are Catholics.
